hero.title: Barcode benchmarks and image recognition
hero.intro: Matched QR generation workflows and a frozen image corpus compare CodeGlyphX, ZXing.Net, ZXing-C++ and QRCoder. Speed, managed allocation and recognition quality are reported separately. The full comparison and the later decoder follow-ups retain separate qualified sources.

sharedHost: Other tasks were active during timing. Comparisons rotate engine order within each fixed cache domain and retain all outliers. This is a shared-host measurement, with no idle-machine or universal performance claim; the evidence records CPU samples before each suite.
recognition: The frozen ZXing Java black-box corpus contains 279 images: 267 positives and 12 negatives. Each reader receives the same preloaded RGBA32 pixels and format hints. Exact payload sets preserve Unicode, newlines and significant spaces; multi-symbol images require every expected payload. Image loading is excluded. QRCoder is generation-only. The Code 128 comparison hint includes GS1-128, matching the physical family in both ZXing readers. This follow-up holds input hashes, hints, oracles and payload scoring fixed.
recognitionLimit: This externally sourced corpus is used during development and regression testing, so it is not a held-out accuracy study. The corpus favors the ZXing ecosystem and is not a representative survey. The same six MaxiCode images now decode correctly; one-symbol scanning is supported, while multiple instances, geometry, mirrored lattices and arbitrary perspective remain unproved. QR and retail photographs retain misses; the supplemental PDF417 results are reported separately. Format-hinted results do not establish default-profile accuracy. Undeclared Shift-JIS QR payloads and an Expanded Stacked oracle with a 54-digit price where GS1 permits at most fifteen illustrate text-policy and scoring limits; unexpected output on a positive image can also reflect an incomplete oracle. Separate retail diagnostics report both recovery outcomes and the additional search cost.
negatives: The fixed supplementary set contains all 25 upstream falsepositives-2 images; six also appear among the twelve main-corpus negatives. These are separate passes, so an overlapping image can finish in one and exhaust its budget in another as host load changes. Correct rejections require scanning to complete. Empty output after a deadline or recognition-budget limit remains inconclusive. The downloadable report also retains alternating previous/current runs across all 31 distinct negative IDs.
generation: QR error correction M, scale 8 and quiet zone 4 are fixed. URL uses version 4, 32 numeric digits version 2, and repeated Japanese/emoji/Polish text version 16. ASCII may use compact modes; multilingual bytes declare UTF-8 ECI without a BOM. Full payload, version, error correction and dimensions are checked outside timing; every batch output is materialized and verified.
adapters: Modules includes encoding and a common one-byte-per-module result. PNG includes encoding and rendering: CodeGlyphX and QRCoder use their own PNG APIs. Both ZXing bindings use the same CodeGlyphX RGBA PNG codec because the tested bindings do not supply a PNG encoder. PNG results compare complete adapter workflows and do not isolate QR algorithms.
allocation: Managed allocation excludes native allocations. A smaller managed-byte count does not establish lower total memory use, especially for ZXing-C++.
decoding: The fixed 19-image timing subset includes a negative, a MaxiCode image supported by both current and previous source, and a four-QR image. Correct-image counts accompany every retained sample. Missed and unfinished decodes remain included. The timing comparison applies to this fixed subset; accuracy on the full corpus differs. Mean managed MiB measures process-wide allocation during the complete batch operation, including runner invocation overhead. Image loading, result evaluation and native allocations are excluded; this is not peak or total memory use. QRCoder has no decoding lane.
methodology: Twelve rotated samples after three warmups, with outlier removal disabled. Generation measures 100-output batches; decode timing measures the complete 19-image subset.

Image effort: CodeGlyphX Robust with a 1500 ms per-image budget; ZXing.Net TryHarder, AutoRotate and TryInverted; ZXing-C++ TryHarder, TryRotate and TryInvert. The other readers have no equivalent cooperative deadline, so search effort is not identical.

Single-result APIs are used for one expected payload. Multiple-result APIs are used for multi-symbol and negative images. Scores compare distinct payload sets, not physical instances with identical payloads.

Physical presentation rules cover Codabar start/stop characters, UPC-A leading zeros, expanded UPC-E, equivalent valid GS1 GTIN/AI element strings and lossless MaxiCode carrier-field presentation alongside exact secondary text. Invalid GS1 oracles remain verbatim. There is no trimming, substring matching or partial-set success.

Corpus revision 33dfdefcb35576612841e614d44ba9edc9aee2b5. Selection takes the first six eligible UTF-8-oracle images per folder by SHA-256 path ordering; binary-oracle fixtures are excluded. The supplementary set contains the same 25 upstream falsepositives-2 images, with all IDs and hashes preserved.
reproduce: The repository's docs/fair-comparisons.md records acquisition, opt-in engine builds and shared-runner commands. Build/Get-DecodeCorpus.ps1 acquires hash-locked fixtures; Build/fair-comparisons.benchmark.ps1 and Build/decode-corpus.benchmark.ps1 declare the measured workloads.
